paragraphs: R. Chiyya bar Avuya said: anyone who has intercourse with a Cuthean woman is as though he had married into idolatry, etc. He also said that he saw Yehoyakim's skull, on which was written, “This, and yet another.” R. Perida's grandfather found a skull at the gates of Jerusalem, with “This, and yet another” written on it. He hid it in his chest, and his wife burned it. Rashi, chapter HaNisrafin, 82a, explains that R. Chiyya bar Avuya was R. Perida's grandfather: Chelek, 104a. Gilgulei Neshamot writes that R. Perida's grandfather repaired Yehoyakim and therefore had pity on him. His wife was of a spark of Athaliah, who hated the royal line, to fulfill “This, and yet another”—although we have written that Rabbi Chutzpit was Yehoyakim's reincarnation; see there, letter pe.
